items.title: Sharks in an aquarium
items.text: Visitors at a South Korean aquarium watched in amazement at a shark swimming in a tank with another shark’s tail hanging out of its mouth. While sharks do not tend to eat others of the same species when they are in captivity and they have regular feeds, experts at the aquarium said that sharks have their own territory, and when they occasionally bump against each other, they bite out of astonishment . The smaller shark which fell prey to its bigger counterpart was a banded hound shark. The bigger beast was a sand tiger shark. Difficult words: tend (to do something regularly), species (a kind of animal), astonishment (great surprise), counterpart (a similar animal). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: Sharks in an aquarium
items.text: At a South Korean aquarium, a shark swam into an even bigger shark, and the bigger shark ate it! For some time, the big shark swam around, and the tail of its prey hung out of its mouth. The visitors of the aquarium looked on in amazement . Sharks do not usually eat each other in captivity , but they have to have their own territory. Difficult words: prey (an animal another animal eats), amazement (surprise, shock), captivity (not free). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Sharks in an aquarium
items.text: This news is from an aquarium . The aquarium is in South Korea. There are sharks in the aquarium. A big shark attacks a smaller shark. The big shark eats the small shark. The small shark hangs out of the big shark’s mouth. Visitors see this. They are shocked. This is rare . Usually, sharks do not eat other sharks. However, sharks can be territorial . Difficult words: aquarium (a place where you can see fish), rare (special, it does not happen often), territorial (when an animal or a person has an area which is his or her area; the animal or person protects the area). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Russell Brand goes to prison
items.text: Following the high-profile conviction of British comedian and actor Russell Brand for rape and sexual assault, UK police chiefs expect more victims to step forward. London’s Metropolitan Police Commissioner stated that successful court verdicts often give additional survivors the confidence to report past abuse, knowing they will be believed. Brand, who previously starred in Hollywood films and was once married to pop singer Katy Perry, faces a lengthy prison sentence after a London court found him guilty of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others. He also faces ongoing investigations regarding additional allegations , including one involving a 16-year-old girl at the time of the incident. British Prime Minister praised the victims for their courage in bringing the horrific crimes to light. As one of Britain’s most prominent public figures convicted of sex offenses in recent years, Brand remains in custody and is awaiting his formal sentencing hearing. Difficult words: conviction (a formal declaration by a court of law that someone is guilty of a criminal offense), allegation (a claim that someone has done something illegal or wrong, typically one made without immediate proof), courage (the ability to do something frightening or difficult without showing fear). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: Russell Brand goes to prison
items.text: British comedian Russell Brand was found guilty of rape and sexual attack in a London court. Following the verdict, police leaders say they expect more victims to come forward with new claims. One of them explained that seeing a famous person held responsible gives other victims confidence to speak up. Brand, a former Hollywood actor once married to singer Katy Perry, now faces a long time in prison. British Prime Minister thanked the brave women who spoke out about his terrible crimes. Police are already looking into other complaints against Brand, including one from a girl who was 16 years old at the time. The 51-year-old former star will go to court for his formal sentencing . Difficult words: rape (the crime of forcing another person to have sex without their consent), victim (a person harmed, injured, or killed as a result of a crime, accident, or other event), sentencing (the official proceeding where a judge gives a verdict). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Russell Brand goes to prison
items.text: A London court says that famous British actor Russell Brand is guilty of big crimes. He hurts four women and must now go to prison for a long time. Police say that more women will likely come and tell their stories now. The police say that it is good that women can speak. People will believe them now. The British prime minister thanks the women who tell the truth about Brand’s bad actions. Police are still looking into other stories about him. Brand will find out his time in prison soon. Difficult words: guilty (when someone is responsible for something bad they do), likely (when something may happen or be true), prime minister (the leader of a government). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Chef fired for refusing to put pineapple on pizza
items.text: An Italian chef in Brisbane, Australia, has been fired for refusing to put pineapple on pizzas, among other reasons. He went to the Fair Work Commission to fight his dismissal, but failed to get his job back. The chef stated that topping pizzas with the tropical fruit was an "insult to his culture". He claimed he was sacked from a restaurant in May after repeatedly refusing his boss's instructions to make pineapple and ham pizzas for diners. His employer contended that the refusal was one of several workplace issues. The commission rejected the chef's application because it was submitted after the deadline. The chef has since found a job at another Italian restaurant. The question of whether pineapple belongs on pizza is a controversial one. It continues to divide public opinion. Pizza purists are aghast at the idea, but it is an established menu staple in many countries. The Hawaiian pizza was reportedly invented in Canada in 1962 after a chef used ham and pineapple as toppings. The restaurant owner expressed his opinion on it. He admitted that while the pizza was not his "absolute favourite," he would not "turn his nose up at it". Many restaurateurs insist that customers should be free to enjoy whatever ingredients and toppings they choose. items.title: Man completes 28-year walk around the world
items.text: A British man has completed an amazing 28-year walk around the world. Former soldier Karl Bushby, 57, arrived home in the city of Hull in England on Monday. He started his adventure in November 1998 in Chile, South America. His plan was to walk all the way home without using cars, boats, buses, trains, or airplanes. During his journey, he travelled about 58,000 kilometres through 29 countries. He crossed frozen seas, deserts, mountains, and jungles. He also faced many dangers. These included encountering polar bears and kidnappers, and spending time in a Russian prison. His journey was expected to take 12 years. However, problems with money, visas, and borders made his trip a lot longer. Thousands of people welcomed Mr Bushby home. He was very happy to finally finish his journey. His mother was waiting outside his childhood home to greet him. Bushby joked: "Sorry to keep you waiting." He also told the cheering crowd that many people around the world had helped him get home. He said he could not have done it alone. Britain's Prime Minister congratulated him on his achievement. He praised Bushby's determination and belief in himself. Bushby told the Guardian newspaper that he wasn't so interested in walking. He said: "It's boring as hell." That didn't stop him walking across four continents. items.title: Study finds majority of pilots nod off mid-flight
items.text: A new report has raised serious concerns about pilot fatigue. The European Cockpit Association (ECA) conducted a survey of nearly 7,200 pilots across 32 countries. It discovered that exhaustion in the cockpit is a widespread and underreported problem. More than three-quarters of respondents said they had briefly dozed off while operating an aircraft in the month before the survey. Almost a quarter of them admitted they continued flying even when they were too tired. Furthermore, half said they had operated a flight when they should have declared themselves unfit for duty. Tiredness can result from long working hours, insufficient rest, and unpredictable schedules. The pilots were very frank in their answers to the survey questions. Many said they were reluctant to report fatigue because they feared punishment or other negative reactions from their bosses. Captain Coen George, a director of the ECA, warned: "When pilots fear career consequences, fatigue goes unreported and the risk returns to the cockpit." Aviation safety experts say exhaustion can impair judgement, slow reaction times and prevent pilots from responding effectively to unexpected in-flight situations. The experts urged airlines to foster a culture in which pilots can report tiredness without fear of repercussions. Carriers should ensure that passenger safety is their top priority. items.title: World-famous London shopping street pedestrianized
items.text: One of London's most famous shopping streets has been pedestrianized. This means no cars, buses, trucks, or motorbikes can enter it. The street is called Oxford Street. It is well known all over the world. It used to be full of traffic. The Mayor of London, Sir Sadiq Khan, decided to make it pedestrian-only. Around one kilometre of the street is off limits to vehicles. However, delivery trucks can use the area between midnight and 7 am. Mayor Khan hopes the pedestrianization will bring more shoppers back to the area. He called it a very important event for London. Mr Khan also plans to plant more trees along the street, create public squares, and add more seats and tables. There have been mixed reactions to the pedestrianization of Oxford Street. Many people support the plan. They are happy that the area will be less polluted. Khan said a traffic-free Oxford Street would "unlock the full potential" of an important area of London and help make a better, greener, and richer London. Around half a million people visit the street every day. However, many Londoners are unhappy that the street has been closed to traffic. Local official Tim Barnes said: "Traffic will be pushed to the small streets nearby causing economic and environmental harm." The Spectator magazine warned that life for car drivers would be harder. items.title: Fake bomb warnings
items.text: A wave of anonymous bomb threats continued to disrupt European aviation on Friday, following at least 25 reported scares across the continent the previous day. Control towers placed a Ryanair flight from Rome to Lisbon under high security alert after they received a call warning of an explosive device on board. The aircraft landed safely in Portugal, where security forces immediately launched thorough inspections. Simultaneously , French authorities confirmed four additional bomb alerts involving planes flying over their airspace, all of which landed safely for emergency checks. Elsewhere, a Wizz Air flight from Prague to Rome was diverted to Venice because of a similar security threat. European law enforcement agencies and judicial police have opened extensive investigations to identify the source of these widespread disruptions. While security teams have found no explosives so far, EU officials stated it remains too early to determine if the coordinated scares are linked. Difficult words: anonymous (made or done by someone whose name is not known or made public), simultaneously (happening, existing, or done at the same time), judicial police (branch of law enforcement responsible for criminal investigations and gathering evidence for legal proceedings). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: Fake bomb warnings
items.text: A series of fake bomb threats disrupted many flights across Europe on Friday. This happened after more than 25 flights faced similar threats on Thursday. One Ryanair plane flying from Rome to Lisbon got a warning about a bomb on board. The plane landed safely in Portugal, where police began searching the aircraft. In France, officials reported four more bomb warnings for planes in their airspace. Another flight from Prague to Rome had to land in Venice because of a safety warning. Thankfully , all planes landed safely, and emergency teams checked them carefully. European police are now investigating who is making these phone calls, but officials don’t know yet if the events are connected. Difficult words: series (several similar events, things, or people which come one after another), bomb threat (a message or call warning that a bomb is placed somewhere), thankfully (luckily). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Fake bomb warnings
items.text: Many planes in Europe get fake bomb warnings on Friday. The day before, 25 other flights get similar warnings. One plane from Rome to Lisbon has a bomb warning, but it lands safely . Police check the plane and find nothing. Four more planes get fake warnings. They fly from France. They land safely. Another plane going from Prague to Rome must land in Venice. Police in Europe are looking for the people who make these phone calls. All planes are safe, but officers are still checking everything to keep people safe when they fly. Difficult words: bomb warning (a message or call warning that a bomb is somewhere), flight (a journey by plane), safely (in a way which is not risky or harmful). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: A footballer dies
items.text: Tragedy has struck Spanish football following the death of Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel at the age of 30. The forward suffered severe head and chest injuries during a heavy collision with FC Andorra’s goalkeeper, who was sent off for the challenge. De Miguel collapsed on the pitch and received emergency treatment while visibly shaken players and fans looked on. Reports indicate he suffered a cardiac arrest in the ambulance on the way to the hospital, where paramedics managed to resuscitate him. Although his condition was initially reported as stable but serious on Monday, his health rapidly deteriorated overnight. Tenerife officially announced his tragic passing early Tuesday morning. The Spanish Football Federation has postponed scheduled Spanish Cup fixtures as the entire football community mourns the loss of the respected player, while authorities begin further investigations into the exact cause of death. Difficult words: cardiac arrest (a sudden loss of heart function, breathing, and consciousness), deteriorate (to become progressively worse in health, quality, or condition), fixture (a sports match or event that has been arranged to take place on a specific date). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: A footballer dies
items.text: Spanish football is in mourning after Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel died at age 30. During a second-division match against FC Andorra, he suffered head and chest injuries in a bad collision with the goalkeeper. De Miguel collapsed on the field and was rushed to the hospital by paramedics, who had to help him after his heart stopped in the ambulance. On Monday, doctors said his condition was serious but stable, and family members came to visit him. But his health got much worse during the night, and his club confirmed his death on Tuesday morning. Everyone at the club is heartbroken, and officials postponed some football matches to show respect for his family and friends. Difficult words: mourning (deep sadness when someone dies), collision (moving object or person striking violently against another), condition (how a person feels and well they are). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: A footballer dies
items.text: A sad event happens in Spanish football. A 30-year-old player named Jesús de Miguel dies after a big game accident. He hits another player hard during a match. He hits his head and chest . Doctors take De Miguel to the hospital quickly. At first, he is not well, but he is stable . But everything changes in the night. On Tuesday morning, his football team says that De Miguel dies. Many players and fans are very sad. Officials stop some matches to remember him and help his sad family. Difficult words: chest (a person’s body between the neck and the stomach), hospital (a building where doctors and nurses look after sick people), stable (when something does not change). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: What happens if you do not brush your teeth for a year
items.text: If you stop oral hygiene , the balance between helpful bacteria and harmful pathobionts in your mouth quickly breaks down. Within just a few days, harmful bacteria multiply and create a sticky layer called dental plaque. This plaque irritates your gums, which can cause bleeding and inflammation , an early stage of disease called gingivitis. Within a month, the bacteria produce strong acids that eat away at tooth enamel and create painful cavities. If left untreated for several months, gingivitis worsens into periodontitis, which damages soft gum tissue and causes gums to pull away from your teeth. After a year without cleaning, chronic infection destroys the underlying bone and causes teeth to wobble and fall out. Even worse, damaged gums allow harmful bacteria to enter your bloodstream. From there, these microbes can travel through the body and worsen serious health conditions, including heart disease, diabetes, and memory disorders like Alzheimer’s. Difficult words: oral hygiene (keeping your mouth clean and free of disease by regular brushing and flossing), pathobiont (a potentially disease-causing microorganism that normally lives harmlessly in the body unless the balance is disrupted), inflammation (when part of the body becomes red, swollen, hot, and often painful as a reaction to injury or infection), enamel (the hard, shiny outer surface layer of a tooth). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: What happens if you do not brush your teeth for a year
items.text: Your mouth needs daily cleaning to stay healthy. If you stop brushing and flossing , bad bacteria grow very fast. In just a few days, sticky plaque covers your teeth, and your gums bleed and swell. This early stage is called gingivitis. After a month, the bacteria break down tooth enamel and form cavities . If you ignore your teeth for a year, the infection gets much worse. Your gums pull away, the bone holding your teeth shrinks, and your teeth can fall out. Even worse, bad bacteria can get into your blood and cause serious health problems in your heart, kidneys, and brain. Brushing twice a day stops these dangerous bugs and protects your whole body. Difficult words: floss (to use a soft thread to clean between the teeth), plaque (a sticky film of bacteria on teeth), enamel (the top layer of a tooth), cavity (a hole in a tooth). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
